papers.title: Single-cell chromatin accessibility atlas decodes bone development, diseases, and regeneration.
papers.abstract: Bone development, homeostasis, and regeneration are governed by complex, dynamic gene regulatory programs, and these processes are disrupted in numerous skeletal diseases. The epigenetic landscape-particularly chromatin accessibility-dictates transcription factor binding and gene expression, which fundamentally shape bone cell fate and function. In recent years, single-cell chromatin accessibility technologies, most notably single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), have revolutionized bone epigenome research and enabled single-cell resolution dissect
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling (primarily scATAC-seq) has been applied to map the epigenetic regulatory landscape of bone development, homeostasis, and regeneration, and how these programs go awry in skeletal diseases. It highlights how single-cell resolution reveals transcription factor binding and gene regulatory programs that dictate bone cell fate and function, providing a framework for understanding skeletal disease mechanisms and informing regenerative strategies.

papers.title: A Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graph for Hypertension With Emotional Comorbidity: Development and Blinded Question-Answering Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) literature on hypertension with anxiety, depression, or insomnia contains descriptions of syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs. A focused knowledge graph can organize these associations and their sources, but its contribution to generated answers requires separate evaluation.
papers.summary: This paper develops a knowledge graph that organizes traditional Chinese medicine concepts—syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs—for hypertension accompanied by anxiety, depression, or insomnia, and links them to their literature sources. The authors then evaluate whether grounding a question-answering system in this graph improves the quality of generated answers using a blinded assessment. The work demonstrates a domain-specific approach to structuring TCM knowledge and testing its utility for retrieval-augmented answering.

papers.title: Whole genome sequencing, assembly, and functional annotation of Hyphopichia burtonii Y951 isolated from Vitis vinifera L. cv Cabernet Sauvignon grape must.
papers.abstract: Hyphopichia burtonii is a non-conventional yeast present in diverse environments including bread, cured meat, grape must, zebra dove droppings and corn weevil. Strains derived from different environments display different traits. However, limited information exists on the genomic diversity of this species. Here we present the genome of H. burtonii Y951 strain isolated from grape must and proven to have antifungal activity against various grapevine fungal pathogens. The genome was sequenced using PacBio long-read technology, and a high-quality de novo genome assembly was generated using the Fly
papers.summary: This study reports a high-quality PacBio long-read genome assembly and functional annotation of Hyphopichia burtonii strain Y951, a non-conventional yeast isolated from Cabernet Sauvignon grape must that shows antifungal activity against grapevine pathogens. The genome provides a foundation for understanding the genetic basis of its antifungal traits and for comparative genomic studies of environmental adaptation in this species.

papers.title: Lessons From CABBI: Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in C4 Crops Through a Vertically Integrated DBTL Framework.
papers.abstract: The global demand for renewable liquid fuels and biobased chemicals has intensified interest in engineering high-biomass C4 grasses to accumulate triacylglycerol (TAG) in vegetative tissues. Achieving this goal requires coordinated solutions across molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment, disciplines that rarely operate within a single research program. The Center for Advanced Bioenergy and Bioproducts Innovation (CABBI) was established to provide this integration through a Design-Build-Test-Learn (DBTL) framework applied to three C4 feedstocks: sacchar
papers.summary: This paper describes the CABBI center's vertically integrated Design-Build-Test-Learn framework for engineering C4 grasses (such as sugarcane, sorghum, and miscanthus) to accumulate triacylglycerol (oil) in vegetative tissues for renewable fuels and biobased chemicals. It highlights how coordinating molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment within a single program accelerates progress toward vegetative oil production. The work offers lessons and a model for interdisciplinary bioenergy crop engineering.

papers.title: OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission.
papers.abstract: Zoonotic viral emergence poses persistent challenges to global health, yet evidence relevant to spillover and cross-species transmission is dispersed across surveillance, epidemiological, experimental, mechanistic, and genomic studies. Here, we present OmniVira (https://omnivira.org/), a curated knowledgebase that transforms literature-derived findings into structured, traceable, and reusable OmniVira Evidence (OVE) records. OmniVira implements an auditable article-evidence framework linking individual findings and supporting text to normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, and relevan
papers.summary: OmniVira is a curated knowledgebase that converts literature on viral spillover and cross-species transmission into structured, traceable evidence records. Each finding is linked to its source text and normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, making dispersed surveillance, epidemiological, and genomic evidence reusable and auditable.

papers.title: Early Prediction and Prognosis in Acute Kidney Injury Using a Biomarker-Aware Transformer: Retrospective Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common, life-threatening complication among hospitalized patients. Timely prediction is crucial for prevention, while accurate prognosis following onset is essential for guiding care. Although electronic health records (EHRs) provide rich longitudinal data, their high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity pose challenges for traditional machine learning.
papers.summary: This retrospective multicenter study develops a biomarker-aware transformer model that leverages longitudinal electronic health record data to predict both the onset of acute kidney injury and its subsequent prognosis. The approach addresses the high dimensionality and temporal complexity of EHR data by incorporating biomarker information into a transformer architecture. Results suggest the model can support earlier intervention and better post-onset care planning for AKI.

papers.title: Meta Mesh Ontology for Cross-Domain Mental Health Knowledge Integration: Development and Evaluation Study.
papers.abstract: Psychiatric diagnostic practice faces persistent challenges in adequately capturing the complexity, heterogeneity, and dynamic nature of mental disorders. Conventional categorical classification systems such as the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) and the International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision (ICD-11) rely on rigid symptom-based criteria that often fail to represent multifactorial etiologies, dimensional symptom profiles, and high rates of comorbidity. Although dimensional models, domain-specific ontologies, and alternative taxonomi
papers.summary: This paper develops a Meta Mesh Ontology designed to integrate mental health knowledge across different domains, addressing the limitations of rigid categorical systems like DSM-5 and ICD-11. The ontology aims to better capture the complexity, heterogeneity, and comorbidity of mental disorders by combining dimensional models and domain-specific ontologies into a unified framework. The study includes development and evaluation of this ontology for cross-domain knowledge integration.

papers.title: scSpatial: an atlas for single-cell spatial omics.
papers.abstract: Single-cell spatial omics (SCSO) has reshaped spatial profiling by enabling simultaneous molecular characterization and spatial mapping at single-cell resolution, providing insights into cellular identities and tissue architecture within native biological contexts. By integrating spatial coordinates with molecular profiles and cell identities, SCSO datasets have been widely used to construct spatially resolved cell atlases, characterize disease-associated tissue remodeling, and map disease-relevant cell populations. However, these SCSO datasets remain fragmented across individual publications,
papers.summary: scSpatial is a new atlas/database that consolidates single-cell spatial omics datasets, which were previously scattered across individual publications. It integrates spatial coordinates with molecular profiles and cell identities to support construction of spatially resolved cell atlases and characterization of disease-associated tissue remodeling. The resource aims to make SCSO data more accessible and reusable for the community.

papers.title: Precision Nutrition and Health Outcomes Across the Lifespan.
papers.abstract: Precision nutrition is an emerging paradigm that seeks to tailor dietary recommendations and interventions based on individual and population characteristics. Although advances in multi-omics, wearable sensors, and artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) have accelerated discovery, translation into practice remains limited by fragmented evidence across life stages and insufficient integration of knowledge regarding systems biology and other influences on health. Nutritional needs, vulnerabilities, intervention opportunities, and response heterogeneity evolve dynamically from preconcep
papers.summary: This review argues that precision nutrition—tailoring dietary advice using multi-omics, wearables, and AI/ML—has advanced rapidly but remains hard to translate into practice because evidence is fragmented across life stages and poorly integrated with systems-biology knowledge. The authors call for a lifespan-oriented framework that accounts for how nutritional needs, vulnerabilities, and response heterogeneity change from preconception onward.

papers.title: Ontology- and Data-Driven Circularity Assessment of Waste-Derived Rigid PVC-u: A Micro-Macro Decision Framework for Sustainable Recycling and Smart Manufacturing.
papers.abstract: The circularity of waste-derived rigid unplasticised poly (vinyl chloride) (PVC-u) is constrained by heterogeneous waste-stream sources, degraded material quality, legacy additives, and inconsistent decision criteria spanning technical, environmental, and economic aspects. In this work, we developed an ontology- and data-driven circularity assessment framework for waste-derived rigid PVC-u recycling systems, built on a Protégé ontology coupled with big data analytics. The framework structures knowledge on materials, recycling processes, process parameters, quality aspects, sustainability measu
papers.summary: The authors developed a framework for assessing how circular (recyclable and sustainable) waste-derived rigid PVC-u is, combining a Protégé ontology with big data analytics to organize knowledge about materials, recycling processes, quality, and sustainability. It aims to support decision-making across technical, environmental, and economic criteria for recycling and smart manufacturing. The work is a decision-support framework rather than an experimental or biological study.

papers.title: WingShape-Warn: A Morphology-Driven Early-Warning Pipeline for Mosquito-Borne Disease Surveillance.
papers.abstract: Environmental stressors-including climate change, urbanisation, and pollution-are increasingly altering the wing morphology of mosquito vectors. These morphological shifts, particularly in wing geometry, can serve as early-warning indicators for mosquito abundance and arboviral disease outbreaks. However, quantitative wing-shape analysis remains underutilised in operational mosquito surveillance and public health early-warning systems. This Technology and Code article presents WingShape-Warn, a reproducible, open-source pipeline that integrates geometric morphometrics, deep learning-based imag
papers.summary: WingShape-Warn is an open-source, reproducible pipeline that combines geometric morphometrics with deep learning-based image analysis to quantify mosquito wing shape from images. The authors propose that wing-shape shifts driven by environmental stressors can serve as early-warning indicators of mosquito abundance and arboviral outbreak risk, aiming to bring quantitative morphometrics into operational surveillance.

papers.title: Comparative Genomic Analysis Reveals Evolutionary Features of Glugea plecoglossi, a Fish-Infecting Microsporidian Parasite of Ayu (Plecoglossus altivelis).
papers.abstract: Microsporidia are obligate intracellular parasites with extensively reduced genomes, yet substantial genomic variation occurs among lineages. Glugea plecoglossi infects ayu (Plecoglossus altivelis) and forms conspicuous xenomas, but its genome characteristics and evolutionary position remain poorly resolved. We generated a genome assembly of G. plecoglossi and compared it with 42 additional microsporidian taxa using phylogenomics, functional profiling, repeat analysis, and multi-copy orthogroup analysis. The 16.71 Mb assembly comprised 59 scaffolds, with a scaffold N50 of 557.5 kb and 78.5% co
papers.summary: This study presents a genome assembly of Glugea plecoglossi, a microsporidian parasite that infects ayu fish and forms xenomas, and compares it with 42 other microsporidian taxa. The 16.71 Mb assembly reveals genomic features and evolutionary relationships within this reduced-genome parasite lineage, providing a resource for understanding microsporidian diversity and host adaptation.

papers.title: An Ontology for Workplace Violence: Protocol to Support Cross-Sector Incident Reporting in Public Services.
papers.abstract: Underreporting is a defining problem in the documentation of workplace violence across public services. This is reinforced by inconsistent, often poor incident descriptions and the absence of a clear, shared nomenclature. Without an ontology-backed structure, similar events are recorded differently across settings or remain uncodable and effectively invisible. Moreover, workplace violence (WPV) is typically registered and studied within sector- and even organization-specific categories and local reporting logics rather than through a shared semantic framework, limiting comparability and cumula
papers.summary: This protocol paper proposes developing a shared ontology for workplace violence (WPV) incident reporting across public services, addressing the problem of underreporting caused by inconsistent terminology and sector-specific reporting categories. The ontology aims to provide a common semantic framework so that similar events are recorded comparably across settings, enabling cumulative and cross-sector analysis. The paper describes the planned methodology rather than reporting completed results.

papers.title: Applications and Future Prospects of Plant Multi-Omics Technologies in Precision Agriculture.
papers.abstract: Against the backdrop of global population growth, intensifying climate change, and limited arable land, ensuring food security and promoting sustainable agriculture have become critical issues. The limitations of conventional agricultural systems are becoming increasingly apparent, creating an urgent need for innovation driven by science and technology. In this context, plant multi-omics technologies serve as the foundational data and technical cornerstone of systems biology and precision agriculture. Integrating multi-level data from genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, epigen
papers.summary: This review argues that integrating plant genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and epigenomics data provides the foundational systems-level information needed for precision agriculture. It surveys current applications of multi-omics in crop improvement and discusses future prospects for using these integrated datasets to address food security under climate change and land constraints.

papers.title: Endogenous APP-Associated Proteomics in Mouse Brain Defines a Candidate Resource for APP Trafficking and Proteostasis Studies.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Affinity proteomics of amyloid precursor protein (APP) is complicated by proteolytic processing, dynamic trafficking, and purification background. We generated a C-terminal 3×FLAG knock-in at the endogenous App locus to establish a cortical affinity-proteomic resource and prioritize APP-associated candidates for further study. Methods: Eight-week-old male homozygous APP-3×FLAG mice on a C57BL/6J background and wild-type littermates were characterized by biochemical and behavioral assays (n = 6 and n = 7 per genotype, respectively). Cortical material from three APP-3×FLAG
papers.summary: The authors created a 3×FLAG knock-in at the endogenous App locus in mice to enable affinity purification of APP and its associated proteins from cortical tissue, providing a resource for studying APP trafficking and proteostasis. They characterized the mice biochemically and behaviorally and generated a candidate list of APP-associated proteins for follow-up. This is a resource-generation study rather than a mechanistic finding.

papers.title: EBV-HSA-RegDB: A database of regulatory interactions between Epstein-Barr virus and human miRNAs.
papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a ubiquitous human herpesvirus associated with various malignancies and autoimmune diseases. MiRNAs play crucial roles in viral-host interactions by regulating gene expression post-transcriptionally. Understanding the regulatory networks between EBV-encoded miRNAs and human miRNAs is essential for elucidating viral pathogenesis and identifying therapeutic targets. We reported the EBV-HSA miRNA Regulatory Database (EBV-HSA-RegDB, https://lbcd.ufpa.br/ebvhsa or  https://lbcd.ia.br/ebvhsa ), an integrated bioinformatics resource that combines comparative sequence analy
papers.summary: This paper presents EBV-HSA-RegDB, a curated database of regulatory interactions between Epstein-Barr virus-encoded miRNAs and human miRNAs, built by integrating comparative sequence analysis with other bioinformatics approaches. The resource aims to help researchers map the viral-host miRNA regulatory network underlying EBV pathogenesis and identify potential therapeutic targets. It is a specialized, web-accessible database rather than a new experimental finding.

papers.title: Comparative Toxicity of Antifouling Paint Particle Suspensions and Dissolved Leachates in the Marine Copepod Tigriopus japonicus.
papers.abstract: Antifouling paint particles (APPs), generated by coating degradation and ship-maintenance activities, are an emerging but poorly characterized source of marine pollution. APPs can release particle-associated and dissolved toxicants, yet their relative contributions to toxicity remain unclear. In this study, environmentally collected APPs were used to prepare two exposure media: an APP suspension containing suspended paint particles and dissolved constituents, and a corresponding membrane-filtered leachate representing the operationally defined dissolved fraction. Their toxic effects on the mar
papers.summary: This study compares the toxicity of suspended antifouling paint particles versus their dissolved leachates in the marine copepod Tigriopus japonicus, finding that both particle-associated and dissolved fractions contribute to harmful effects. The work highlights that antifouling paint particles are an underappreciated pollution source whose toxicity cannot be attributed solely to dissolved chemicals.

papers.title: Unlocking the full potential of spatial omics in plants: practical challenges, solutions, and a path forward.
papers.abstract: Spatial omics technologies provide new opportunities for plant biology by enabling molecular profiling within structurally intact tissues, revealing spatially organized cell states, developmental gradients, and regulatory interactions. While spatial transcriptomics has driven early advances, the field is rapidly expanding toward integrated spatial multi-omics by combining single-cell and spatial transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data. These approaches offer new opportunities to study development, physiology, and plant biotic and abiotic interactions in spatially preserved
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial omics technologies can be applied to plant biology, moving beyond spatial transcriptomics toward integrated multi-omics that combine transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data within intact tissues. It outlines practical challenges specific to plants and proposes solutions and a roadmap for broader adoption.

papers.title: Crystalline silica particles exposure modulated miRNA expression profiles in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells.
papers.abstract: Occupational and environmental exposure to crystalline silica particles is a major global health concern linked to silicosis, pulmonary fibrosis, autoimmune disease, and lung cancer. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate gene expression post-transcriptionally and are emerging as potential effect biomarkers of exposure in human biomonitoring studies. To identify intracellular and extracellular miRNAs responses to silica-particle exposure in human THP-1 derived macrophages, differentiated THP-1 derived macrophages were exposed to 0-300 µg/mL crystalline silica particles for 24 h. Cytotoxicity was assessed
papers.summary: This study exposed human macrophage-like THP-1 cells to crystalline silica particles and profiled changes in microRNA expression both inside cells and in the extracellular environment. The authors identify silica-responsive miRNA signatures that could serve as biomarkers of occupational silica exposure, linking particle exposure to downstream inflammatory and fibrotic pathways.

papers.title: Cutibacterium acnes induces T-cell extracellular traps with distinct proteome programs.
papers.abstract: Cutibacterium acnes is a common skin commensal associated with acne pathogenesis. In this study, we investigated whether acne-associated (denoted as CA) (HL043PA1) and healthy skin-associated (denoted as CH) (HL110PA3) C acnes strains differentially induce extracellular traps (ETs) in human neutrophils (neutrophil ETs) and T helper 17 cells (T-cell ETs [TETs]) and defined their proteomic and functional properties. Both strains triggered rapid ET release from neutrophils and T helper 17 cells. However, whereas neutrophil ETs displayed a conserved proteomic profile regardless of the strain, TETs
papers.summary: This study shows that both acne-associated and healthy skin-associated strains of Cutibacterium acnes trigger rapid extracellular trap release from human neutrophils and Th17 T cells. While neutrophil extracellular traps had a conserved proteomic profile regardless of strain, T-cell extracellular traps (TETs) exhibited distinct proteome programs depending on the bacterial strain. This suggests TETs may contribute to acne pathogenesis through strain-specific functional properties.

papers.title: Reframing QSP: AI-Driven Multi-Modal Data as a New Measurement Layer.
papers.abstract: Quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) provides a mechanistic framework for integrating biological and pharmacological knowledge in drug development. Simultaneously, advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in multi-modal data analysis, are transforming how biological information is derived. I argue that AI should not be viewed as a data integration tool, but as a new layer of quantitative measurement generation. This reframing positions QSP as a foundational model of biology, used here in a conceptual rather than technical sense, and AI as a source of quantitative inputs.
papers.summary: This perspective argues that AI-driven multi-modal data analysis should be reframed not as a tool for integrating data into quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models, but as a new layer that generates quantitative measurements. In this view, QSP serves as a foundational conceptual model of biology, while AI supplies the quantitative inputs that feed it. The paper is a conceptual commentary rather than a technical or empirical study.

papers.title: PDBe-SIFTS: An open-source tool for Structure Integration with Function, Taxonomy, and Sequences, featuring improved alignment, scoring scheme, and accelerated search.
papers.abstract: Structure integration with function, taxonomy and sequences (SIFTS) provides residue-level mappings between UniProt Knowledgebase sequences and Protein Data Bank structures and has historically been generated through internal Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe) pipelines. Here, PDBe-SIFTS is presented as a fully open-source, locally deployable implementation of this mapping framework. The pipeline combines fast, scalable sequence search using MMseqs2, an improved bounded scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and residue-level mapping refinement based on backbone connectivity. PDBe-SIFT
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: PDBe-SIFTS is a new open-source, locally deployable tool that maps UniProt protein sequences to Protein Data Bank structures at residue-level resolution. It improves on the original SIFTS pipeline by using MMseqs2 for fast sequence search, a better bounded scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and backbone-connectivity-based refinement of residue mappings. This makes high-quality structure-function mapping accessible to any lab without relying on internal PDBe infrastructure.

papers.title: MAOMAO: an ontology-guided FAIR resource for harmonized peptide toxicity data.
papers.summary: MAOMAO is a new ontology-guided resource that harmonizes peptide toxicity data according to FAIR principles, making it easier to find, compare, and reuse toxicity information for therapeutic peptides. It provides a structured, standardized framework for integrating heterogeneous peptide toxicity datasets, which should support safety assessment and machine-learning applications in peptide drug discovery.

papers.title: Implementing the ILAE 2025 seizure taxonomy in medical software.
papers.abstract: The International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE), working via a multidisciplinary task force, has issued a position paper with updated seizure classification guidelines (2025) replacing its previous guidance (2017), establishing a revised de-facto standard for clinical assessment and classification of epileptic seizures. The 2025 model simplifies the system, making it easier to adopt in different clinical settings while also clarifying the taxonomic rules, the definition of consciousness, and the application of phenomena-based descriptors. As a result, clinical practitioners, technologists, an
papers.summary: This paper describes how to implement the ILAE 2025 seizure taxonomy—an updated clinical classification standard that simplifies seizure categorization and clarifies rules around consciousness and symptom descriptors—within medical software systems. It provides practical guidance for translating the revised taxonomy into computational tools used by clinicians and technologists.

papers.title: HuRInterDB: A Database Exploring the Landscape of lncRNA-Protein Interactions.
papers.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) possess diverse biological functions and play key regulatory roles in biological processes by interacting with other biomolecules, such as proteins, RNAs, and the genome. High-throughput RNA-interaction experiments have generated large volumes of lncRNA-protein interaction records. The fragmented deposition of these records across disparate public databases complicates unified retrieval and integrative analysis. Here, we present HuRInterDB (Human lncRNA-Protein Interaction Database), a comprehensive and standardized database that focuses on human lncRNA-protein in
papers.summary: HuRInterDB is a new standardized database that consolidates human lncRNA-protein interaction records scattered across public databases, enabling unified retrieval and integrative analysis. It addresses the fragmentation of high-throughput RNA-interaction data by providing a comprehensive, curated resource for studying lncRNA regulatory functions.

papers.title: CfDNA methylation profiling in blood following moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury using brain cell type-enriched signatures: A pilot study.
papers.abstract: The human brain consists of diverse cell types that collaboratively perform complex functions and form intricate neuronal networks. When traumatic brain injury (TBI) occurs, multiple molecular pathways involving diverse cell types are activated in response to injury. Understanding how brain cell composition is altered during TBI may help improve patient outcomes. Upon brain trauma, neurovascular disruption leads to the release of brain-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) into peripheral blood. The tissue-specific DNA methylation patterns in this cfDNA have the potential to serve as candidate markers
papers.summary: This pilot study profiled cfDNA methylation in blood from patients with moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury, using brain cell type-enriched methylation signatures to infer which brain cell types contribute to circulating cfDNA after injury. The approach suggests that cell-type-specific methylation patterns in cfDNA could serve as candidate biomarkers for assessing brain cell composition changes and injury response in TBI.

papers.title: Integrating cure and care in Alzheimer's disease: a systems perspective for precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease remains a major global health challenge, with limited disease-modifying therapies and a rapidly growing societal burden. Although amyloid and tau remain central to the field, current evidence also implicates neuroinflammation, immune dysregulation, vascular dysfunction, and host-microbe interactions in disease pathogenesis. These developments support a broader systems framework, but simply combining additional disciplines or data modalities does not by itself preserve the dynamic biology or lived experience of disease. Artificial intelligence multi-omics, and digital biomar
papers.summary: This perspective argues that Alzheimer's disease research should move beyond amyloid and tau to a systems-level framework incorporating neuroinflammation, immune dysregulation, vascular dysfunction, and host-microbe interactions. The authors propose integrating multi-omics, AI, and digital biomarkers to support precision medicine that combines cure-oriented and care-oriented approaches. It is a conceptual synthesis rather than a primary data study.

papers.title: How AI-based techniques for brain tumour diagnosis can address data variability.
papers.abstract: Data variability in medical imaging of tumors refers to the inconsistencies in Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Computational Tomography scans caused by heterogeneous tumor biology, varying scanner hardware, and subjective human interpretation. This variability creates significant challenges for accurate diagnoses, treatment tracking, and AI model development. Although the variability in medical imaging data for diagnostic and prognostic purposes is a challenge for AI methods applied to other types of tumors as well, it is particularly problematic when the analysis involves gliomas and glioblast
papers.summary: This perspective article discusses how data variability in brain tumour imaging—arising from heterogeneous tumour biology, differing scanner hardware, and subjective human interpretation—poses major challenges for AI-based diagnosis, especially for gliomas and glioblastomas. It outlines how AI techniques can be adapted to address this variability and improve diagnostic accuracy and treatment tracking.
